title: Prototype Chain Walker & Distance Calculator
problemStatement: Implement `getPrototypeDepth(obj)` that traverses an object's prototype chain and returns the number of hops until `null` is reached. If `obj` is null or undefined, return 0.
interviewTrap: Using `__proto__` directly is deprecated. Always prefer `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)`.

testCases.name: Standard object literal has depth of 1 (Object.prototype -> null)
Object created with Object.create(null) has depth 0
Inherited chain depth reflects hierarchy
testCases.testFn: const parent = {}; const child = Object.create(parent); return getPrototypeDepth(child);

details.name: Standard object literal has depth of 1 (Object.prototype -> null)
Object created with Object.create(null) has depth 0

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Every JS object has an internal `[[Prototype]]` link. Property lookup walks this chain until the property is found or `null` is reached (`Object.prototype.__proto__ === null`). Modifying a property on an instance creates an 'own property' shadowing the prototype's property.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for [[Prototype]] Traversal to Object.prototype and null.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), [[Prototype]] Traversal to Object.prototype and null is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Using `__proto__` directly is deprecated. Always prefer `Object.getPrototypeOf(obj)`.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.
